chunks: And in the narration of Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
"that if he has a stay in Mecca and wishes to fast the seven [days of Qada], he should leave fasting for the duration of his travel to his family or for a month, then he should fast."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), the source of the narration

ai.seo_question: How does one adjust the fasting schedule for making up missed days while traveling or staying in Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) clarifies the flexibility in making up missed Ramadan fasts (Qada) for a traveler residing in Mecca, allowing them to pause fasting for a duration equivalent to their journey home or a full month. It highlights the Shia juristic principle of easing religious obligations during travel, distinguishing between the strict prohibition of fasting while traveling and the leniency applied to the makeup period. This ruling underscores the practical application of 'rukhsa' (dispensation) within the broader framework of maintaining spiritual discipline.
